content.text: {"concept_key":"c10-biology-aerobic-anaerobic-respiration","title":"Aerobic vs Anaerobic Respiration","quick":"Aerobic respiration needs oxygen and breaks food fully, releasing lots of energy plus CO2 and water. Anaerobic respiration happens without oxygen, breaks food partially, releases less energy, and produces alcohol or lactic acid instead.","full":"Think of a kirana shop owner counting cash: if he has full light (oxygen), he counts every note carefully and gets the complete total (full energy) - that's aerobic respiration, happening in mitochondria, giving about 38 ATP, producing CO2 and water as waste. If the light goes off suddenly (no oxygen), he counts roughly in the dark, gets much less accurate total (less energy, only 2 ATP), and makes mistakes - that's anaerobic respiration, happening in cytoplasm, producing lactic acid in muscles (causing cramps) or alcohol+CO2 in yeast. Same starting material (glucose), different oxygen availability, different end products and different energy output.","traps":["Writing only 'one needs oxygen, other doesn't' without mentioning end products","Forgetting that lactic acid forms in human muscles during anaerobic respiration","Mixing up energy amounts - saying anaerobic gives more energy than aerobic"],"misconception":"Children think anaerobic respiration is just 'respiration without air' with same energy output, not realizing it's incomplete breakdown giving far less energy.","parent_questions":[{"q":"What happens in your muscles when you run fast and feel cramps?","expected_answer_hint":"Anaerobic respiration occurs due to lack of oxygen, producing lactic acid which causes cramps."},{"q":"Which type of respiration gives more energy and why?","expected_answer_hint":"Aerobic, because glucose is completely broken down using oxygen into CO2 and water."}],"check_question":{"q":"During heavy exercise, muscle cramps occur due to buildup of which substance?","options":["Lactic acid","Carbon dioxide only","Oxygen"],"correct_index":0,"right_feedback":"Correct! Lactic acid builds up during anaerobic respiration in muscles when oxygen is insufficient.","wrong_feedback":"Not quite. During oxygen shortage, muscles do anaerobic respiration producing lactic acid, causing cramps."},"illustration":{"scene_prompt":"A shopkeeper counting cash at a kirana shop, shown once in bright daylight and once during a power cut with a dim candle.","labels":[{"text":"Aerobic","position":"top-left"},{"text":"Anaerobic","position":"top-right"},{"text":"Oxygen","position":"left"},{"text":"No Oxygen","position":"right"}]}}
